annotations.title: To litle ones.
annotations.text: By this place euery vulgar artificer may not preſume that God hath reuealed al truth to him, and therfore refuſe to be taught of the learned. for Chriſt did not aftervvard endew fiſhers and vulgar men nor any other with the gifts of wiſdom and tonges, without their induſtrie, ſtudy, and teaching. though at the beginning, of great prouidence he did it, that it might be cleere to the world, that al Nations vvere conuerted to him, not by perſuaſion of cunning Orators or ſubtil Diſputers, but by the plaine force of his grace and truth, which S. Auguſtine counteth greater then al other miracles. <mn>◦</mn> Further we are taught by this place, that the poore humble obedient children of the Church knovv by their faith the high myſteries of Chriſtes Diuinity, and his preſence in the B. Sacrament, and ſuch like: rather then Arius, Caluin, and other like proud Scribes and Phariſees.

notes.text: The humble vnlearned Catholike knoweth Christ better then the proud learned Heretike.

annotations.title: This doe.
annotations.text: Not by faith only, but by keeping Gods commaundements we obtaine life euerlaſting: not onely by beleeuing, but by doing. ◦ The heretikes ſay that it is impoſſible to keepe this commaundement of louing God with al our hart. But the Scriptures giue vs examples of diuers that haue kept and fulfilled it, as far as is requiſite in this life. 3. reg. 14, 8. 2. Par. 15, 15. Ps. 118, 10. Ecclci. 47, 9, 10. 4 Reg. 20, 3. 5. Luc. 1, 5. And if it were impoſſible to keepe it, and yet by Chriſt propoſed for the meane to obtaine life euerlaſting, he had mocked this Lavvyer and others, and not taught them.

notes.text: The commaundements possible to be kept.

annotations.title: Halfe dead.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> <mn>[2]</mn> Here is ſignified man vvounded very ſore in his vnderſtanding and free-wil, and al other povvers of ſoule and body, by the ſinne of Adam: but yet that neither vnderſtanding, nor free-vvil, nor the reſt, were extinguiſhed in man or taken away. The Prieſt and Leuite, ſignifie the Law of Moyſes: this Samaritane, is Chriſt the Prieſt of the new Teſtament: the oile and wine, his Sacraments: the hoſt, the prieſts his miniſters. Vvhereby is ſignified, that the Law could not recouer the ſpiritual life of mankind from the death of ſinne, that is, iuſtifie man: but Chriſt onely, who by his paſſion and the grace and vertue thereof miniſtred in and by his Sacraments, iuſtifieth, and increaſeth the iuſtice of man, healing and abling free-vvil to doe al good workes.

notes.text: The parable of the wounded man, explicated.
Conc. Araus. 2 cap. 25. to. 1. Conc. Conc. Trid. Sess. 6. c. 1.

annotations.title: Marie the beſt part.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Tvvo notable examples, one of the life Actiue, in Martha: the other of the life Contemplatiue, in Marie: repreſenting vnto vs, that in holy Church there ſhould be alwaies ſome to ſerue God in both theſe ſeueral ſorts. The life contemplatiue is here preferred before the actiue. the Religious of both ſexes are of that more excellent ſtate. and therfore our Proteſtants haue wholy abandoned them out of their common wealth, which the true Church neuer wanted. But to ſay truth, they haue neither Martha nor Marie. our Lord geue them grace to ſee their miſerie. If ours were not anſwerable to their profeſſion, or were degenerated, why haue they no new ones? if our Churches Votaries vowed vnlawful things, Chaſtitie, Pouertie, Obedience, Pilgrimage: what other Votaries or lawful vowes haue they? For, to offer voluntarily by vow (beſides the keeping of Gods commaundements, wherevnto we are bound by precept and promiſe in our Baptiſme) our ſoules, bodies, goods, or any other acceptable thing to God, is an acte of ſoueraine worſhip belonging to God onely: and there was neuer true religion without ſuch vowes and Votaries. <mn>[2]</mn>If there be none in their whole Church that profeſſe contemplation, or that vow any thing at al to God voluntarily, neither in their bodies nor in their goods: God and the world know they haue no Church nor religion at al.

notes.text: The Contemplatiue or Religious life, better then the Actiue and secular.
